propositions: Frontier exclusion blocks rendered inert by fence design; model did not suppress re-searches listed in treated frontier context, contradicting the hypothesis that explicit exclusion data would reduce overlap.
Frontier blocks acted as signposts, raising measured overlap by directing model back to files already read, increasing re-search rates rather than decreasing them.
Treatment arm showed higher re-search overlap than control on both corpus tickets (45c1: B 44.4% vs A 25%; 8d74 cumulative: B 80% vs A 50%), failing the 30% relative reduction gate on every ticket.

Cache-seeding manifest (standard locust resume behavior) already eliminates dominant redundancy from re-proving credited criteria; remaining re-grounding of unproven criteria cannot be suppressed by data-shaped frontier blocks in untrusted fence.
Token cost for treatment arm increased (45c1 B +34% output; 8d74 B +21.9% input) without overlap reduction, adding expense without benefit.
